paragraphs: This is This Week in Congress, from Power to the People, for the week ending Saturday, November 14th, 2026.
This briefing is read by a computer voice. Every fact in it comes from public records at Congress.gov, the House Clerk and Senate.gov.
The Senate held six recorded votes this week.
On Monday, the Senate voted to begin debate on the Survivor Justice Tax Prevention Act, 73 to 25.
On Tuesday, the Senate voted to take up the Survivor Justice Tax Prevention Act, 62 to 21.
On Thursday, the Senate voted to end debate on the nomination of Gregory Carl Cook, 50 to 27.
Also on Thursday, the Senate confirmed Gregory Carl Cook to be U.S. District Judge for the Northern District of Alabama, 49 to 27.
Also on Thursday, the Senate voted to end debate on the nomination of Daniel Desmond Domenico, 51 to 27.
Also on Thursday, the Senate voted to end debate on the nomination of Anna St. John, 49 to 26.
The House held nine recorded votes this week.
On Monday, the House passed two bills under a fast-track rule that needs two thirds: House bill 3978, 397 to 2; and the American Enrichment Deployment Act, 394 to 3.
On Tuesday, the House adopted House resolution 1650, 215 to 209.
On Wednesday, a motion to bring House resolution 1247 out of committee succeeded, 245 to 175.
Also on Wednesday, the House passed House bill 1013, 295 to 128.
On Thursday, the House adopted House resolution 1247, 271 to 135.
Also on Thursday, the House passed the Major Richard Star Act, 392 to 18.
The House also held two other votes. Every vote is listed in the app.
The Senate also passed 13 measures without a recorded vote. Among them were the Carson City Public Land Correction Act and the Route 66 National Historic Trail Designation Act.
The House also passed five measures without a recorded vote.

Four bills became law: the Choices for Increased Mobility Act of 2026, the America's National Churchill Museum National Historic Landmark Act, the Bankruptcy Threshold Adjustment Act, and the National Taxpayer Advocate Enhancement Act of 2025.
Coming up, the Senate next meets Monday, November 16th, 2026. The plan: convene at 3:00 p.m. The House has 17 bills on its schedule for the week of Monday, November 9th, 2026.
That's this week in Congress. You can read every bill and every vote in the app. Thanks for listening.
